issues.title: Operator scaling mistaken for a new interpolation space

failure_location.quote: However, the application of the second-derivative operator, required to solve the PDE, fundamentally alters the interpolation space and degrades this stability.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since our basis functions are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on the extended domain, this new basis is explicitly $\{\phi_j(x) = \lambda_j w_j(x)\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that applying the second derivative fundamentally changes the interpolation space and thereby degrades its Lebesgue stability. The old basis formula and Poisson calculation instead establish φ_j=λ_jw_j with λ_j>0, hence span{φ_j}=span{w_j}; interpolation at fixed nodes and its Lebesgue constant depend on this span, not on nonzero rescaling of its coordinates. Diagonal scaling can affect coefficient-matrix conditioning, but it does not produce the claimed new interpolation space.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted mechanism for a stability dichotomy between basis interpolation and Poisson interpolation is false, although diagonal operator scaling can still affect algebraic conditioning.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the quoted claim by the basis-invariant statement that phi_j = lambda_j w_j with lambda_j nonzero leaves both the interpolation space and its Lebesgue constant unchanged. If operator scaling is discussed, identify its possible effect as coefficient-matrix conditioning rather than interpolation-space stability.
issues.why_classification: This is a substantive conceptual conflation, not a transcription error. The repair is local and a closely related conditioning statement survives, so neither global reconstruction nor major mathematical loss is necessary. It nevertheless withdraws the claimed Lebesgue-stability mechanism, which is meaningful loss and rules out a minor classification.

issues.title: False logarithmic bound for restricted sine interpolation

failure_location.quote: While not identical to classical Chebyshev points, such nodes exhibit the same characteristic clustering near the interval endpoints.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing a=πδ/(L+2δ), the old change of variables gives θ-nodes uniformly spaced on [a,π-a] and ξ-nodes ξ_k=cos θ_k. Because sin θ is bounded below by sin a, all ξ-gaps, including the endpoint gaps, are of order 1/N; the nodes therefore lack Chebyshev endpoint clustering. More decisively, for s=π/2-a, the logarithm of a central cardinal polynomial evaluated halfway between the first two nodes has limiting rate s^{-1}∫_0^s log(2 cos t)dt>0. The bounded sine prefactor in the old formula does not remove this exponential growth. Hence the Lebesgue constant cannot satisfy a C log N bound for fixed δ.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed logarithmic stability of the one-dimensional restricted basis and the derived O((log N)^d) multidimensional basis theorem are invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the stated fixed extension and uniform physical grid, replace thm:basis_bound by a proved exponential-growth lower bound, or at minimum by an explicit statement that no C log N bound holds, and revise the dependent tensor-product theorem so that it no longer asserts O((log N)^d) stability. A logarithmic theorem may instead be proved for a deliberately clustered node family, but it must be presented as a different interpolation scheme.
issues.why_classification: The cardinal-polynomial calculation contradicts the theorem's central logarithmic rate and shows exponential growth for the advertised uniform grid. Retaining that grid therefore requires reversing the stability conclusion, while retaining the logarithmic rate requires replacing the substantive node contract. No local same-guarantee repair exists, so every complete resolution entails major mathematical loss.

issues.title: Impossible simultaneous sine-smallness lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The phase increment is θ_{k+1}(N)-θ_k(N)=πLN/((L+2δ)(N-1)), which tends to d=πL/(L+2δ)∈(0,π). If |sin θ_k| and |sin θ_{k+1}| are at most ε_N=e^{-cN}, each phase lies within arcsin ε_N of an integer multiple of π. Their difference must then lie within 2 arcsin ε_N of πZ. This is impossible because the increment converges to d, whose distance from πZ is positive. The contradiction already uses k=0 and k=1, so no subsequence can satisfy the stated maximum bound.
issues.overall_effect: The number-theoretic lemma and its appendix restatement are false, and the old proof of super-polynomial Poisson growth that invokes the lemma is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete KeyLemma and its appendix restatement. To retain the dependent super-polynomial Poisson theorem, replace the entire highest-mode argument by a separately proved exponential cardinal-function or restricted-frame near-null construction and rederive the theorem from it; otherwise the dependent theorem must also be withdrawn. Changing only constants or the subsequence is inadequate.
issues.why_classification: The nonvanishing limiting phase increment makes the all-grid maximum estimate impossible for every subsequence. No recognizably comparable statement about the prescribed phases and highest-frequency mode retains its central quantifier or exponential conclusion. Recovering the downstream theorem by a different witness does not preserve the recorded lemma itself, while abandoning the theorem causes further major loss; hence the issue is serious.

issues.title: False degree-uniform restriction norm

failure_location.quote: Then there exists a constant $C_R$, which depends only on the geometry of $I$ and $\tilde{I}$ but is independent of the polynomial degree $M$, such that for any $g \in P_M$:

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $I=(0, L)$ be a fixed interval and $\tilde{I}=(-\delta, L+\delta)$ be a fixed extension for some $\delta > 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Let θ=π(x+δ)/(L+2δ) and a=πδ/(L+2δ). The trigonometric polynomial g_M(x)=(1+cos θ)^M has degree M. On I, its magnitude is at most (1+cos a)^M, while on the extension segment where 0≤θ≤a/2 it is at least (1+cos(a/2))^M. Since 1+cos(a/2)>1+cos a, the ratio of the two L2 norms grows exponentially with M. Thus no geometry-only constant C_R can be independent of degree, and the appendix's asserted C/K extrapolation bound cannot hold.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous-to-physical-domain norm bridge used to obtain N-independent lower singular-value bounds fails. Consequently, the old constant- and variable-convection stability theorems and their multidimensional extension are not established by their proofs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the degree-uniform restriction lemma and its appendix proof by a valid Remez-type estimate with its unavoidable degree dependence, which is exponential in the worst case, and propagate that dependence through every listed theorem. This removes the N-independent singular-value bounds and the resulting polynomial Lebesgue conclusions. Preserving those conclusions would instead require a newly defined stabilized or regularized trial space and new uniform stability proofs.
issues.why_classification: The counterexample rules out any geometry-only constant on the full fixed-extension polynomial spaces. Propagating the correct exponential factor destroys the central polynomial-stability guarantees throughout the affected chain, while avoiding that loss requires reconstructing the method and proof around stabilization or regularization. Thus no complete route avoids both major loss and global new architecture.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Assuming the discretization is sufficiently stabilized (e.g., via oversampling $M \ge \beta N$) such that the quadrature aliasing error is controlled

issues.title: Invalid square-grid norm equivalence
issues.failure_explanation: For the N grid points x_i, the product T_N(x)=∏_{i=1}^N sin(π(x-x_i)/(L+2δ)) is a nonzero trigonometric polynomial of degree at most N and vanishes at every x_i. Its sampled sum is therefore zero while its continuous L2 norm is positive. Thus the cited Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund lower bound is being used without the necessary sample-count versus bandwidth restriction.
issues.overall_effect: The old proofs do not obtain an N-uniform discrete lower bound for the square collocation matrices, so their polynomial convection-diffusion stability conclusions remain unproved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the mode bandwidth from the sample count, impose a proved stable-sampling condition such as at least 2N+1 suitably weighted samples for the full degree-N trigonometric space, and replace the square solve by the corresponding oversampled least-squares or stabilized map. State a valid Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequality for the actual image space and redo its use in each listed one- and multidimensional stability theorem; no N-mode, N-point lower bound may remain.
issues.why_classification: An exact nonzero polynomial vanishing at all N nodes rules out the square-grid inequality, so a citation or constant adjustment cannot repair it. Constant-factor oversampling and the associated least-squares reformulation require a substantive but standard contained reconstruction of the discrete step. They preserve a recognizably comparable method, operator class, stability rate, and asymptotic sample complexity, making the issue moderate rather than minor or serious.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The discrete G\r{a}rding inequality therefore fails for the unstabilized square system, and uniform stability requires stabilization (e.g., $M > N$).

issues.title: Undefined extended-domain coefficient norm

failure_location.quote: Let the convection coefficient $k(x) \in C^1(I)$ satisfy the coercivity condition $\norm{k'}_{L^\infty(\tilde{I})} < 2/C_P^2$

issues.failure_explanation: Membership k∈C1(I) defines k and k' only on the physical interval, so the quantity ||k'||_{L∞(tilde I)} in the same hypothesis has no defined value. The proof explicitly invokes lem:cont_coercivity, whose valid hypothesis is k∈C1(tilde I), making the intended correction unambiguous.
issues.overall_effect: The variable-coefficient theorem has an ill-defined hypothesis and cannot invoke its stated coercivity lemma literally, although its intended domain assumption is clear.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace k in C^1(I) by k in C^1(tilde I), so that the displayed L-infinity norm and the hypothesis of lem:cont_coercivity are defined on the same extended interval. No proof change is needed.
issues.why_classification: The old sentence already evaluates k' on the extended interval, and the explicitly invoked coercivity lemma requires exactly C^1 regularity there. These two source features uniquely force the missing tilde on I; the literal alternative is ill-defined and makes no coherent broader promise. The correction is therefore transcriptional.
